key_insight: CORNETO’s reliability when inferring biological networks from multi-omics data is not uniform: it operates in distinct robustness regimes shaped by prior knowledge and data availability. Regularization and biological context also influence how well the framework can be reused.
problem_solved: The study examines when a previously developed biological network inference framework remains robust across different data and biological settings.
method: Study the reusability of CORNETO for learning biological networks from multi-sample, multi-omics data.
Assess how data availability and prior biological knowledge relate to inference robustness.
Examine the roles of regularization and biological context in reliable reuse.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the findings emphasize that reusing a network inference framework requires checking its data, prior-knowledge and regularization requirements. Robustness in one biological setting should not be assumed to transfer to another.
visual_elements: Conceptual regime map with data availability and prior knowledge as axes, illustrating differing robustness conditions.
Pipeline diagram: multi-sample omics data plus prior knowledge → CORNETO → inferred biological network.
Four-factor graphic highlighting data availability, prior knowledge, regularization and biological context.
Side-by-side network illustrations showing stable versus variable inferred connections.
paper_title: Reusability report: multi-sample omics network inference operates in distinct robustness regimes defined by prior knowledge and data availability
paper_authors: Xabier Martínez-de-Morentin, Sumeer A. Khan, Itziar Cenzano, Robert Lehmann, Alberto Maillo
